title: Sales Administrator
description:
Sales Administrator

Salary: £30,000 per annum

Hours: Monday to Friday 8.45am to 5.30pm, finishing early at 5pm on Fridays

We are looking for a responsible, organised and motivated Sales Administrator to join this growing international business.

This is a varied role for someone who takes pride in getting the detail right, enjoys solving problems and is comfortable dealing directly with customers and suppliers.

You will be joining a young, enthusiastic and supportive admin team, but they're looking for someone with a mature approach to their work someone who can be relied upon to take ownership of a task, manage their priorities and see things through properly.

There is also plenty of opportunity to learn and develop. For the right person who wants to progress, the role can grow as your knowledge, confidence and responsibilities increase.

What s on offer:
- £30,000 per annum
- Bonus scheme rewarding company and individual performance
- 22 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing to 23 days after three years
- Healthcare cash plan
- Pension with company contributions matched up to 5%
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Regular company social events
- A friendly, supportive working environment
- Exposure to customers and suppliers around the world
- Genuine opportunity to develop and progress within a growing business

What you'll be doing as Sales Administrator:
- Responding to enquiries and communicating with customers in the UK and overseas
- Preparing quotations throughout the sales and order process
- Researching products and sourcing solutions to unusual customer requirements
- Negotiating with suppliers and placing purchase orders
- Processing customer orders accurately and efficiently
- Organising international shipments and working with freight companies
- Monitoring orders and proactively dealing with delays or problems
- Taking ownership of customer requirements through to completion
- Working closely with the wider sales and operations team

What you ll bring:
- Experience in sales administration, customer service, order processing or a similar commercial role would be useful, but attitude and approach are equally important.
- Reliable and responsible, with a mature attitude towards work
- Highly organised and able to prioritise when several things need attention
- Naturally detail-focused and someone who checks their own work
- Comfortable taking ownership rather than waiting to be reminded
- A practical problem solver who enjoys finding answers
- Confident and professional when dealing with customers by telephone and email
- Comfortable working independently while also being a good team player
- IT confident
- Interested in learning and developing your commercial knowledge
- Ambitious to progress as you gain experience

title: Finance Officer
description:
Finance Officer

Location: Beccles

Salary: FTE salary of £27,274 - £32,046 per annum Pro-rata salary of £19,350 - £22,735 per annum

Vacancy Type: Permanent, Part Time(26.25 per week, 5 days a week)

STARTING 1 ST JANUARY 2027

Sapientia Education Trust is seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and experienced Finance Officer to join our school-based Finance Team. The Trust is an expanding multi-academy trust with 14 primary and 9 secondary schools, and the finance operation that supports these schools is based across the Trust s secondary schools, with this role based at Beccles High School.

Beccles High School is a vibrant, inclusive community where every student is known, supported and inspired. Since joining Sapientia Education Trust in September 2024, it has embraced a new era, one rooted in ambition, collaboration and student-centred learning. Students tell us that they value the way lessons are delivered and the strong relationships that exist in school between students and staff. This is only possible because of the school s small size and the belief and confidence in every student as an individual.

This post offers an opportunity to work in the growing finance team with responsibility for the whole school finance function - processing invoices, dealing with supplier, customer and parent queries, statement reconciliations for various schools and the wider trust. The ideal candidate will possess strong team working skills, the ability to communicate effectively with a variety of staff and be a resilient problem solver. Support for training (e.g. AAT) will be offered should the post holder wish to undertake professional qualifications.

PERSON SPECIFICATION

The professional competencies expected of the Finance Officer are:
- Be a flexible and enthusiastic team player that is adaptable and resilient in managing and executing their daily responsibilities;
- Have good communication skills in person and in writing to respond to staff, students and outside agencies whilst maintaining confidentiality;
- Be organised and able to manage, plan and complete daily and weekly tasks in a busy office environment;
- Be familiar with the use of, or prepared to learn how to use, a variety of IT Systems (including Sage Intacct).

The qualifications and experience required of the Finance Officer are:
- Experience of working in a busy finance environment;
- Previous purchase/sales ledger experience;
- Maths and English GCSEs grade 4-9;
- AAT qualified or currently studying (desirable).

JOB SPECIFICATION

General Responsibilities

The Finance Officer is responsible for the maintenance of the school s finance system and records in accordance with the Trust s Financial Rules & Procedures. Ensuring that the school s transactional finance is delivered in an efficient and effective manner to meet the school needs. Staff may look after more than one school and this is subject to change based on the evolving needs of each of the Trust s schools.

The post holder will have access to and be responsible for confidential information and documentation. They must ensure confidential or sensitive material is handled appropriately and accurately.

The post holder shall participate in the Trust s programme of Performance Management and Continuing Professional Development; and the post-holder will be required to comply with the Trusts Code of Conduct for Staff and Volunteers.

Specific Responsibilities

A non-exhaustive list of specific responsibilities for the role is below and you will be required

to undertake other duties and responsibilities as may reasonably be required.
- Act as the primary point of contact for all finance queries for relevant school(s)
- Process school orders ensuring compliance with the Trust s Financial Rules and Procedures
- Process invoices received ensuring correct authorisation of expenditure
- Reconcile supplier statements to accounting records, including leading on one or more Trust wide supplier account as account champion
- Reconciling school bank accounts, credit cards and any petty cash held
- Raise relevant school sales invoices
- Manage the school s online payment system (e.g. ParentPay or Wisepay)
- Chasing outstanding invoices with customers and escalating to the Trust s credit control function where appropriate
- Assisting budget holders to effectively cost and manage school related funds (e.g. trips, lettings, buses, productions)
- Recording fund recharges (e.g. Pupil Premium Grant) once authorised by appropriate budget holders

The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the business, supporting colleagues and helping to maintain a positive and sociable working environment.

The ideal candidate will be professional, dependable and confident managing financial records and administrative systems, whilst also bringing energy, initiative and excellent interpersonal skills to the role.

As the Finance and Office Coordinator, duties will include:
- Managing day-to-day financial administration
- Coordinating office systems, supplies, contracts, records and relationships with external suppliers and support providers.
- Providing administrative and document support
- Supporting recruitment
- Organising team and client events
- Maintaining and updating the company website
- Supporting the company's LinkedIn presence
- Providing administrative support for projects
- Acting as a central point of contact within the office

An ideal candidate for the Finance and Office Coordinator will have:
- Previous experience in finance administration, office administration or a varied coordination role.
- Strong organisational skills
- Confidence handling invoicing, expenses, timesheets and financial records.
- Strong Microsoft 365 skills, particularly Excel and Word.
- Excellent communication skills, verbal and written.

Interviews will take place in Newmarket, following a registration process by PureKat Consultancy Ltd. If we have not responded to your application within 3-5 days, unfortunately you have not been successful on this occasion, but please feel free to contact us for other opportunities. PureKat Consultancy Ltd is acting as an Employment Agency for this permanent vacancy.

title: Receptionist / Care Navigator
description: eccles Medical Centre is looking to recruit a receptionist/care navigator to join our team on a part-time basis, for 20 hours a week. The care navigation team plays a vital role in supporting the administrative operations of Beccles Medical Centre. As a care navigator, you will often be the first point of contact for patients entering the practice, providing high-quality customer service and handling a wide range of patient enquiries on a daily basis. Excellent communication skills, professionalism, and a patient-centred approach are essential for success in this role. You will work under the direct supervision of the care navigation team leader, and contribute to the efficient day-to-day running of a busy medical centre that supports nearly 20,000 patients. You will be trained in care navigation as a foundation to any role at BMC which means that you will be the first line to the patient and will take I.C.E (ideas, concerns and expectations) from patients as trained, and care navigate to the right place, right person, right time, right resource using in-house protocols and procedures and online consultation tool when available. It is important in all roles across the practice that attention to detail, listening skills and teamwork are paramount. Whilst staff can work in differing roles, BMC encourages staff to work in an integral way across the whole of the practice. Duties and responsibilities include: Deliver care navigation as a core function of the role, acting as the first line of contact for patients. Use the I.C.E. model (ideas, concerns, expectations) to gather essential information from patients. Ensure patients are directed to the right place, right person, at the right time, utilising in-house protocols, procedures, and online consultation tools as appropriate. Provide consistently high standards of customer service and maintain professionalism in all patient interactions. Work collaboratively across the wider practice, supporting colleagues in a flexible and integrated manner. If you would like to find out more information about this role, please do not hesitate to get in contact with us.
